items.stem: Define a heterogeneous mixture.
items.answer: A mixture with physically distinct parts and non-uniform composition
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A heterogeneous mixture – a mixture with physically distinct parts and non-uniform composition.

items.stem: Which of the following is a heterogeneous mixture?
items.answer: oil and water
items.markingKey: (d) Oil and water is a heterogeneous mixture. The others: brass – a homogeneous mixture; sugar in water – a homogeneous mixture; soda water – a homogeneous mixture.

items.stem: Why is air considered a mixture and not a compound?
items.answer: Its components (nitrogen, oxygen, etc.) keep their properties, are present in varying proportions and can be separated by physical methods such as fractional distillation of liquid air.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: variable composition/properties retained. 1 mark: physical separation.

items.stem: Classify these as a heterogeneous mixture or a homogeneous mixture: muddy water, brass, air, oil and water.
items.answer: A heterogeneous mixture: muddy water, oil and water. A homogeneous mixture: air, brass.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A heterogeneous mixture: muddy water, oil and water. A homogeneous mixture: air, brass.

items.stem: Classify these as a mixture or a pure substance: milk, mercury, ice, carbon dioxide, wood.
items.answer: A mixture: milk, wood. A pure substance: carbon dioxide, ice, mercury.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A mixture: milk, wood. A pure substance: carbon dioxide, ice, mercury.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a heterogeneous mixture?
items.answer: salt solution
items.markingKey: (d) Salt solution is a homogeneous mixture, not a heterogeneous mixture. Each of the others (muddy water, kerosene and water, sand and iron filings) is a heterogeneous mixture.

items.stem: A sample with a sharp melting point is most likely:
items.answer: a pure substance
items.markingKey: (d) a pure substance.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a heterogeneous mixture?
items.answer: vinegar
items.markingKey: (d) Vinegar is a homogeneous mixture, not a heterogeneous mixture. Each of the others (sand and iron filings, muddy water, kerosene and water) is a heterogeneous mixture.

items.stem: Which of the following is a pure substance?
items.answer: distilled water
items.markingKey: (a) Distilled water is a pure substance. The others: milk – a mixture; air – a mixture; sea water – a mixture.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a homogeneous mixture?
items.answer: muddy water
items.markingKey: (a) Muddy water is a heterogeneous mixture, not a homogeneous mixture. Each of the others (brass, soda water, air) is a homogeneous mixture.

items.stem: Classify these as a heterogeneous mixture or a homogeneous mixture: sand and iron filings, salt solution, brass, milk of magnesia.
items.answer: A heterogeneous mixture: milk of magnesia, sand and iron filings. A homogeneous mixture: brass, salt solution.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A heterogeneous mixture: milk of magnesia, sand and iron filings. A homogeneous mixture: brass, salt solution.

items.stem: Milk of magnesia is a colloid. What type of colloid is it?
items.answer: sol
items.markingKey: (d) Dispersed phase solid, dispersion medium liquid: sol.

items.stem: Which of the following is a true solution?
items.answer: salt in water
items.markingKey: (b) Salt in water is a true solution. The others: muddy water – a suspension; shaving cream – a colloid; sand in water – a suspension.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A suspension is stable.
Reason (R): Particles of a suspension settle on standing.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A false; R true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A solution contains 25 g of common salt in 150 g of water. Calculate the concentration in terms of mass by mass percentage of the solution.
Name the dispersed phase, the dispersion medium and the type of colloid in milk of magnesia.
items.answer: Dispersed phase: solid; dispersion medium: liquid; type: sol.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each for phase and medium, 1 mark type.

items.stem: Classify as a suspension or a true solution: salt in water, sugar in water, muddy water, chalk powder in water, flour in water.
items.answer: A suspension: chalk powder in water, flour in water, muddy water. A true solution: salt in water, sugar in water.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A suspension: chalk powder in water, flour in water, muddy water. A true solution: salt in water, sugar in water.

items.stem:
Read: Sahil prepared three mixtures in beakers: A – 30 g of salt in 200 g of water; B – a spoonful of chalk powder in water; C – a few drops of milk in water. A torch beam was passed through each in a dark room.
(i) In which beakers will the path of light be visible? (ii) Which mixture will settle on standing? (iii) Find the mass by mass % of salt in A. (iv) Classify A, B and C.
items.answer: (i) B and C (C shows the Tyndall effect; B scatters too, but settles). (ii) B. (iii) 30/230 × 100 = 13%. (iv) A: true solution; B: suspension; C: colloid.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: A solution contains 36 g of common salt in 320 g of water. Calculate the concentration in terms of mass by mass percentage of the solution.
8 g of urea is dissolved in water to make 250 mL of solution. Find the mass by volume percentage.
items.markingKey: Mass by volume % = mass of solute ÷ volume of solution × 100 = 8/250 × 100 = 3.2%.

items.stem: 5 g of urea is dissolved in water to make 400 mL of solution. Find the mass by volume percentage.
items.markingKey: Mass by volume % = mass of solute ÷ volume of solution × 100 = 5/400 × 100 = 1.25%.

items.stem: Which mixture shows the Tyndall effect?
items.answer: Milk diluted with water
items.markingKey: (a) Milk diluted with water.

items.stem:
Read: Meera prepared three mixtures in beakers: A – 20 g of salt in 100 g of water; B – a spoonful of chalk powder in water; C – a few drops of milk in water. A torch beam was passed through each in a dark room.
(i) In which beakers will the path of light be visible? (ii) Which mixture will settle on standing? (iii) Find the mass by mass % of salt in A. (iv) Classify A, B and C.
items.answer: (i) B and C (C shows the Tyndall effect; B scatters too, but settles). (ii) B. (iii) 20/120 × 100 = 16.7%. (iv) A: true solution; B: suspension; C: colloid.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: 4 g of urea is dissolved in water to make 100 mL of solution. Find the mass by volume percentage.
items.markingKey: Mass by volume % = mass of solute ÷ volume of solution × 100 = 4/100 × 100 = 4%.

items.stem: 10 g of urea is dissolved in water to make 500 mL of solution. Find the mass by volume percentage.
items.markingKey: Mass by volume % = mass of solute ÷ volume of solution × 100 = 10/500 × 100 = 2%.

items.stem: Which method is best for separating pure copper sulphate from an impure sample?
items.answer: crystallisation
items.markingKey: (b) Crystallisation: pure crystals form on cooling a hot saturated solution, impurities stay in solution.

items.stem: Which method is best for separating mud from water?
items.answer: sedimentation and decantation
items.markingKey: (c) Sedimentation and decantation: heavy particles settle and the clear liquid is poured off.

items.stem: Why does a washing machine dryer remove water from clothes?
items.answer: It spins rapidly (centrifugation); water is thrown out through holes while clothes are held by the drum.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: spinning. 1 mark: water forced out.

items.stem: Name the method used to separate mud from water and explain the principle on which it works.
items.answer: Sedimentation and decantation; heavy particles settle and the clear liquid is poured off.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: method. 1 mark: principle.

items.stem: Name the method used to separate different coloured dyes in black ink and explain the principle on which it works.
items.answer: Chromatography; components move at different rates on absorbent paper.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: method. 1 mark: principle.

items.stem: Describe, step by step, how you would separate a mixture of salt, sand and ammonium chloride.
items.answer: Heat (sublimation) to remove ammonium chloride; add water and filter to remove sand; evaporate the filtrate to get salt.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per correct step in a correct order (3 marks).

items.stem: Why is crystallisation better than evaporation for purifying copper sulphate?
items.answer: Some solids decompose or char on heating to dryness, and soluble impurities remain with the solid in evaporation
items.markingKey: (d) Some solids decompose or char on heating to dryness, and soluble impurities remain with the solid in evaporation.
options: Some solids decompose or char on heating to dryness, and soluble impurities remain with the solid in evaporation

items.stem: Which method is best for separating different coloured dyes in black ink?
items.answer: chromatography
items.markingKey: (c) Chromatography: components move at different rates on absorbent paper.

items.stem: Describe, step by step, how you would separate a mixture of chalk powder, sugar and iron filings.
items.answer: Magnet removes iron; dissolve in water, filter out chalk; evaporate or crystallise to get sugar.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per correct step in a correct order (3 marks).

items.stem: Chromatography is used to:
items.answer: separate colours in a dye and detect drugs in blood
items.markingKey: (b) separate colours in a dye and detect drugs in blood.
options: separate colours in a dye and detect drugs in blood

items.stem: Ethanol boils at 78 °C and acetone at 56 °C. Which method would you use to separate a mixture of the two, and which liquid distils first?
items.answer: Fractional distillation; acetone distils first.
items.markingKey: (a) Difference = 22 K, less than about 25 K, so fractional distillation; the lower-boiling acetone distils first.

items.stem: Why is the spot of ink placed above the solvent level in paper chromatography?
items.answer: If it is below, the ink would dissolve directly into the solvent in the beaker instead of rising up the paper with it.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: placed above. 1 mark: reason.

items.stem: Methanol boils at 65 °C and ethanol at 78 °C. Which method would you use to separate a mixture of the two, and which liquid distils first?
items.answer: Fractional distillation; methanol distils first.
items.markingKey: Difference = 13 K, less than about 25 K, so fractional distillation; the lower-boiling methanol distils first.

items.stem: Ethanol boils at 78 °C and water at 100 °C. Which method would you use to separate a mixture of the two, and which liquid distils first?
items.answer: Fractional distillation; ethanol distils first.
items.markingKey: Difference = 22 K, less than about 25 K, so fractional distillation; the lower-boiling ethanol distils first.

items.stem:
Read: At a refinery near Mathura, crude oil is heated and its vapours pass up a tall column. Petrol vapours condense near the top, kerosene and diesel lower down, and heavy oils at the bottom.
(i) Name this method. (ii) On what property does it depend? (iii) Why do fractions with lower boiling points collect near the top? (iv) Name another mixture separated by the same method.
items.answer: (i) Fractional distillation. (ii) Differences in boiling points. (iii) The column is cooler at the top, so only vapours with low boiling points rise that far before condensing. (iv) Liquid air (nitrogen, oxygen, argon).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Why is fractional distillation, not simple distillation, used to separate oxygen and argon from liquid air?
items.answer: Their boiling points (−183 °C and −186 °C) differ by only 3 K, far less than about 25 K, so a fractionating column is needed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: small difference. 1 mark: fractionating column.

items.stem: Water boils at 100 °C and methanol at 65 °C. Which method would you use to separate a mixture of the two, and which liquid distils first?
items.answer: Simple distillation; methanol distils first.
items.markingKey: (d) Difference = 35 K, more than about 25 K, so simple distillation; the lower-boiling methanol distils first.

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

A is false, but R is true.

items.markingKey: (c) A new substance forms, often with gas, heat or colour change.
